1._section_summary: This section presents construct validity evidence for the Dutch BAS-2 (Body Appreciation Scale-2), demonstrating good convergent validity through significant correlations with appearance satisfaction, functionality satisfaction, self-esteem, and optimistic life orientation, and significant negative correlations with self-objectification and BMI. Incremental validity was assessed using hierarchical regression analyses with a sample of 306 participants, showing that BAS-2 scores made significant incremental contributions to predicting both self-esteem and optimistic life orientation beyond appearance and functionality satisfaction alone.

0._section_summary: This procedure section describes a study conducted between September 2014 and October 2015 where female participants fluent in Dutch were recruited from two universities in the Netherlands (Maastricht University and VU University Amsterdam) via campus advertisements and online recruitment systems. Participants completed an online survey, provided electronic informed consent, selected compensation options (research credit or gift certificate entry), and were debriefed, with ethics approval from Maastricht University.
